text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. In supervised learning, the most common type, we give the computer labeled training data. This means each example includes both the input and the correct answer. The computer uses this data to build a model, which is essentially a mathematical pattern. Once the model is built, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. For example, a model trained on photos of cats and dogs can predict whether a new photo shows a cat or a dog. The quality of the model is measured by its accuracy, or how often its predictions are correct. More training data usually leads to better accuracy.
